memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is how you are to build it: The ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide and thirty cubits high. Make a roof for it, leaving below the roof an opening one cubit high all around. Put a door in the side of the ark and make lower, middle and upper decks. - Gen 6:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Noah exact measurements - length, width, height, an opening, a door, three decks. Nothing is left to guesswork. This was an enormous undertaking, a vessel the size of which the world had never seen, and Noah had no rain, no flood, no evidence yet - only God's word and God's plan.

There is a quiet beauty in these detailed instructions. God's plan for salvation is not vague or careless; it is precise and sure. And Noah's task was simple in one sense: not to improve on the design, not to question it, but to follow it exactly. Faith obeys the instructions of God even when they seem strange or the reason is not yet visible.

Notice too the single door in the side of the ark. There was only one way in. When the time came, everyone who was saved entered through that one door. It quietly foreshadows Jesus, who said, "I am the door. If anyone enters by me, he will be saved" (John 10:9).

For us, the call is to trust and obey God's revealed way of salvation rather than inventing our own. Noah did not need to understand everything; he needed to trust the One giving the instructions. God's way may not always make sense to us at first, but it is always precise, always trustworthy, and always for our rescue.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you willing to obey God even before you understand why?
- Have you entered through the one door of salvation, Jesus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the faith of Noah - to trust and obey Your instructions even when I cannot yet see the reason. Thank You that Jesus is the one door into salvation.
